name: Sheldon Whitehouse

issue_poll.name: Pell Center / Embold Research Rhode Island Survey, Sept 16–20, 2024 (876 likely voters)
issue_poll.note: Most important issue question. Democracy and economy tied at 22%; taxes, climate and education tied at 2%; foreign policy (1%) was the next item.

issues.position: Supreme Court term limits and a binding ethics code
issues.note: No Senate floor vote on Court term limits or an ethics code this term.

issues.position: First-time homebuyer tax credit; expand Low-Income Housing Tax Credit
issues.note: H.R.1 included a 12% LIHTC expansion; he opposed the package. No vote on a homebuyer credit.

issues.position: Pass the 2024 bipartisan border security agreement
issues.note: The bipartisan agreement was not brought back for a floor vote this term.

issues.position: Codify Roe; legal abortion in all 50 states

votes.question: Cloture on the motion to proceed

issues.note: No vote on codifying Roe this term; rated on an abortion-restriction bill instead.

issues.position: Keep and build on Medicare drug-price negotiation
issues.note: H.R.1 widened the orphan-drug exemption from Medicare negotiation.

issues.position: Universal background checks; assault weapons and high-capacity magazine ban
issues.note: No recorded Senate floor vote on these measures this term.

issues.position: Raise taxes on income over $400K to fund Social Security
issues.note: H.R.1 made 2017 tax cuts permanent, including for top earners.

issues.position: Keep Inflation Reduction Act clean-energy and offshore wind credits

caveats: Economy rated on his housing tax-credit proposals (RI Current questionnaire); H.R.1 counted as inconsistent because it expanded LIHTC, following the nh-hassan precedent.
Abortion rated on the S.6 Born-Alive cloture vote, which tests his position only indirectly.
Gun position comes from the Giffords PAC endorsement (Feb 2024), not a statement in his own words.
Roll calls (H.R.1 #372, S.6 #11) taken from usquery and other trackers because senate.gov was unreachable.
